    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

    According to recent reports, there are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    It has been revealed that they’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    According to recent reports, you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel intends before choosing.

    In a recent development, each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    It has been revealed that latest lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    It has been revealed that global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

    Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    According to recent reports, through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

    If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

    If you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

    In a recent development, this community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Industry observers note that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    This community would be an excellent choice if your upcoming travels include several of these airports, even if dining isn't the main reason for your trips. If dining out is one of your favorite activities, check out the best credit cards for restaurants.

    Active Escapes focuses on airports in outdoor-oriented destinations that are all in the U.S., save one. Benefits here are:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    Industry observers note that while these airports are gateways to national parks and other natural attractions, you don’t have to be an outdoor enthusiast to benefit. Like before, don’t let the heading sway you. Rather, consider the destinations before you decide.

    In a recent development, families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:.

    Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    According to recent reports, through Dec. 31, 2027, these destinations qualify for bonus points and status points:.

    This community may be especially valuable if you regularly book award flights for children 12 and under. Even if you don't travel with kids, it could be worth considering if its qualifying airports align better with your travel aims than those of other communities.

    Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:.

    Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

    Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

    Two Travel Now discounts per year for 30% off one-way refundable Y-class fares on Alaska Airlines, booked within four days of departure for travel to, from or within Alaska.

    Ship cargo within Alaska for $49 plus tax (weight, size and content limits apply).

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Baggage benefits don’t combine with other free checked bag allowances, such as those that come with some Alaska credit cards. However, they apply to everyone traveling on the same reservation.

    It has been revealed that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus offers:.

    According to recent reports, while this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel plans — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

    Hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:.

    Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

    Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

    Don’t be persuaded by the names of the communities. Look a little deeper, because there’s a lot of overlap between destination lists. Compare the options against your upcoming travel plans.

    You can change communities once per calendar year, so you aren’t locked in to your initial choice indefinitely. However, switching communities resets your destination-challenge progress, but you’ll retain any points you’ve already earned.

    If your home airport (or one you visit frequently) is already on a community’s list, you may have an easier time earning points. Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

    It has been revealed that finally, pay attention to airport codes. For example, Tokyo’s Narita (NRT) and Haneda (HND) appear on different community lists. Latest York’s qualifying airport is JFK, while it is DCA in Washington, D.C. If you have a choice between airports, check which one qualifies for your community’s challenge.

    • The midterm election results sent a shudder through the defense industry.

    • Sources indicate that RTX (RTX -1.32%) is one of only two major U.S.-based defense stocks whose shares have risen since the midterm elections.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Halley – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than RTX ›.

    The midterm election results sent a shudder through the defense industry.

    President Donald Trump is proposing a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027, but time is running out to pass the budget in a lame-duck Congress. Next year's Congress is likely to take a more critical look at defense spending.

    Sources indicate that RTX (RTX -1.32%) is one of only two major U.S.-based defense stocks whose shares have risen since the midterm elections. There are four reasons why RTX is the one defense stock I'd buy over Lockheed Martin (LMT -1.11%).

    Unlike many of its peers, the tech giant is positioned to continue doing well because its revenue streams also include sales of parts and equipment to commercial airlines, providing a cushion if next year's Congress slashes the defense budget.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, RTX has three segments, but only one of them is a pure-play defense segment: Raytheon, which makes air and missile defense systems. The other two segments, Pratt & Whitney and Collins Aerospace, make defense and commercial airline products. Pratt & Whitney makes aircraft engines for civilian and military aircraft, while its Collins Aerospace segment makes aircraft systems, including avionics, navigation systems, and flight controls for commercial and defense aircraft.

    Lockheed Martin's shares, on the other hand, are down more than 3% since the elections because it has little commercial sales, with more than 69% of its revenue coming from the U.S. government.

    It has been revealed that RTX reported double-digit revenue and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) growth in the third quarter. Revenue was reported as $25 billion, up 11% year over year, and adjusted EPS grew by 33% over the prior year to $2.26. The company also raised full-year guidance. It says it expects 2026 sales of $97 billion to $97.5 billion, up from earlier estimates of between $95 billion and $96 billion. It also raised adjusted EPS from $7.10 to $7.25, up to $7.65–$7.75.

    Adjusted segment operating margins expanded by 310 basis points in the third quarter, and because aircraft engine maintenance and spare parts carry higher profit margins than initial equipment sales, RTX's installed base of commercial engines and avionics acts as a compounding cash-flow machine independent of Capitol Hill.

    Pratt & Whitney's commercial aftermarket sales jumped 21% year over year, while Collins Aerospace's adjusted operating profit surged 50%.

    In a recent development, lockheed Martin also had a strong quarter, with revenue rising 11% year over year, to $20.7 billion and EPS of $7.97, up 14% from the same period last year. However, because so much of its revenue lately is tied to Iran war spending, that could slow at any time.

    According to recent reports, RTX reported a backlog of $340 billion in the third quarter, including $164 billion in defense sales and $176 billion in commercial sales. That provides a great deal of stability for investors looking at the company's long-term potential, as it represents three years' worth of revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that just in the third quarter, Raytheon booked nearly $59 billion in defense awards, including production contracts for Tomahawk missiles and air-to-air missiles. Even with Democrats soon to control Congress, global demand for air defense and munitions makes these multiyear contracts highly resilient.

    Lockheed Martin's backlog is smaller at $292 billion, and all of that is tied to defense contracts.

    According to recent reports, the tech giant raised its quarterly dividend by 7.4% this year to $0.73 per share, the 32nd consecutive year it has increased its dividend. The dividend yield is an above-average 1.42%, and while that's lower than Lockheed Martin's 2.39% yield, RTX's streak of raising dividends is eight years longer.

    In addition, over the past three years, RTX has increased its dividend by more than 23%, while Lockheed has raised its dividend by just over 9%.

    RTX stands out as a stronger buy than Lockheed Martin right now largely because its balanced business model insulates it from post-midterm political turbulence on Capitol Hill.

    RTX's greater commercial footprint not only provides a steady buffer against congressional scrutiny, but also fuels a high-margin aftermarket engine and spare-parts business that acts as a compounding cash-flow engine independent of Pentagon appropriations.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    Recent findings suggest that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Industry observers note that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Sources indicate that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    Industry observers note that if PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index revealed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you proposal to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    Sources indicate that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a upcoming home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Recent findings suggest that » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    Recent findings suggest that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.
